title: The Disciple
notes: This chunk is strong: it opens with a precise lexical definition from Isaiah, chains the three cannot-gates to the marks of discipleship, and closes the arc from baptism into the Name to the sealed forehead with clean symbolic consistency. The law-positive stance and density of proof-texts are intact and assertive. Residual issues are limited: one house-style sentence-open with And, a presenter-style 'word to weigh' cue, and one incomplete clause after a semicolon that leaves the Matthew 5:17 allusion dangling. No AI vocabulary, no doctrine rewrites needed, and the modern contrast 'growth curves' is deliberate rather than defective. Surgical fixes restore flow without thinning the voice.

proposals.old: And the covenant one is baptized into has stated content:
proposals.new: The covenant into which one is baptized has stated content:
proposals.summary: Remove forbidden sentence-initial And and repair the relative clause.
proposals.rationale: Author prose may not open with And; the original also lacks a relative pronoun, which the rewrite supplies without changing meaning.

proposals.old: _Indeed_ is the word to weigh: it is spoken to men who had just *believed* (John 8:30-31) — believed as a profession believes: His word accounted factual and worth trusting, an assent even __“the devils”__ manage, who __“believe, and tremble”__ (James 2:19).
proposals.new: _Indeed_ is spoken to men who had just *believed* (John 8:30-31) — believed as a profession believes: His word accounted factual and worth trusting, an assent even __“the devils”__ manage, who __“believe, and tremble”__ (James 2:19).
proposals.summary: Remove presenter cue 'the word to weigh'.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids director cues such as 'Weigh the'; the cut keeps the claim and the following evidence intact.

proposals.old: He kept the law — perfectly: __“Which of you convinceth me of sin?”__ (John 8:46); not to destroy but to fulfil (Matthew 5:17).
proposals.new: He kept the law — perfectly: __“Which of you convinceth me of sin?”__ (John 8:46). He came not to destroy but to fulfil (Matthew 5:17).
proposals.summary: Complete the dangling clause after the semicolon.
proposals.rationale: The original leaves 'not to destroy but to fulfil' without a subject or finite verb; the rewrite restores a full sentence while preserving the two citations and the claim.
